data.ruling: The refutation stands, and it is about this function. V75 treats both faults as continuous, including a short to the port's 8.7 V supply pin (the F16 HV ceiling, Research.md:544). It then derives its series-resistance lower bounds from the short to ground only: 275 Ohm = 3.3 V / 12 mA and 142 Ohm = 3.4 V / 24 mA. For the 8.7 V short it computes only the current into the 3.6 V clamp. V75 puts the clamp on the gate element's side of the resistor. So while the element drives the line low, the node sits at VOL, well under 3.6 V. The clamp does not conduct, and the driver sinks (8.7 - VOL) / R. Pad-driven line at 275 Ohm: (8.7 - 0.5) / 275 = 29.8 mA. That is 2.5 times the 12 mA highest drive setting in Table 1436, and the resistor dissipates 245 mW, not the 95 mW V75 states. 244-driven line at 142 Ohm: (8.7 - 0.55) / 142 = 57.4 mA. That exceeds the SN74LVC244A's +-50 mA absolute maximum IO (SCAS414AG 5.1) and its 24 mA recommended IOL (5.3). With VOL at 0.8 V (125 °C) it is 55.3 mA, still over 50 mA. So V75's lower bounds do not survive the fault V75 itself sets. Bounds that keep the recommended current are (8.7 - 0.5) / 12 mA = 683 Ohm and (8.7 - 0.55) / 24 mA = 340 Ohm. The 683 Ohm bound conflicts with V75's own servo-configuration ceiling, which is R <= 331 Ohm at Vs = 0 by V75's nodal formula: 1 / (3.3e-3 / 0.8 - 1.1e-3) = 330.6 Ohm. The verifier wrote the expression as 3.3e-3 / (4.125e-3 - 1.1e-3), a typo; the 331 Ohm result is right. IOBoard.md:536 states that nothing else in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line. The failure comes from this function's fault case and resistor values, not from any part's lifecycle, maker or LCSC identity, so the scope is function.
data.evidence: RP2350 datasheet, build-date 2025-07-29, Table 1436 Digital IO: VOL max 0.5 V at IOVDD = 3.3 V, with IOL = 2, 4, 8 or 12 mA depending on setting (12 mA is the highest); VIL max 0.8 V at IOVDD = 3.3 V. SN74LVC244A SCAS414AG (revised June 2026): 5.1 IO continuous output current +-50 mA absolute maximum; 5.3 IOL 24 mA at VCC = 3 V; VOL 0.55 V max at IOL = 24 mA and VCC = 3 V (0.8 V over -40 to +125 °C). IOBoard.md:531 at e13f5f60: 3 wires per output lead (signal, ground, rail). IOBoard.md:536: no requirement in the tree limits the current into a shorted signal line at an output connector. Research.md:544 F16: the HV ceiling cuts the port off above 8.7 V. Research.md:635 V75: the Answer column reads "for research (owner, 2026-09-28)"; the owner has not answered, so V75's continuous-fault premise is the claim's own. Recomputed: 8.2 V / 275 Ohm = 29.8 mA and 244.5 mW; 8.15 V / 142 Ohm = 57.4 mA; 8.2 V / 12 mA = 683 Ohm; 8.15 V / 24 mA = 340 Ohm; the servo-mode ceiling at Vs = 0 is 330.6 Ohm.
